title: One tree, a whole year
_map: The four seasons (Y1). Big idea: weather and day length change across the year. Creative: watch the farm through a year in one minute; what changes? Plan what to plant when.
_story: Steve watches one apple tree for a whole year, sped up. Blossom, green leaves, orange leaves, bare branches. Days get longer then shorter. When should we plant?
_stepChain: a year (days-weeks-months) → the year has four parts called seasons → spring, summer, autumn, winter → the tree changes → days are long in summer, short in winter → plan planting

talk.ask: What are the four seasons, in order?

talk.goodAnswer: in summer. In winter they're short and it gets dark early.

handsOn: Pick one tree near you. Take a photo of it every month for a year. Put the photos in order. What changed?

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: I'm going to watch my apple tree for a whole year! Sped up, very fast.
A year has four parts, each about 3 months long. Each part is called a season. Spring: blossom. Summer: green leaves. Autumn: leaves turn orange and fall. Winter: bare branches, and maybe snow.
Look at the yellow bar. It shows how many hours of daylight there are.

question.onRight: Yes. In summer the sun is up for about 16 hours. In winter, only about 8.

1.hint: When does it stay light until bedtime?
1.say: In winter it gets dark early, with only about 8 hours of daylight. In summer it's light for about 16 hours.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: When should I plant my seeds? Spring is warm and getting lighter, perfect for seeds. Then they grow all summer, and I pick pumpkins in autumn!

rule.ask: Can you say the four seasons in order? Say them out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: The four seasons are spring, summer, autumn and winter. The days are longest in summer and shortest in winter.

bonus.prompt: Bonus: in Australia, it's summer at Christmas! Why?
choices: They're on the other side of the world
bonus.reveal: They're on the other half of the Earth, so their seasons are the opposite way round to ours.
